messages:
ivy: Noticed a pattern: intermittent p95 spikes (~15ms) for GPU-hosts in rack r33 when tenant-99 runs many small inference calls. Baseline clear otherwise. Dashboard: https://grafana.internal/d/egress/r33

rohan: Could be small-packet pps storm from their telemetry sidecar + NIC coalescing. Any tcpdump or nic stats?

ivy: Quick host dump from r33-node4:
```
eth0 tx_q_len: 48
p95_rtt: 14.8ms
irq_rate: 120k/s
softirq_balance: skewed to cpu2
top_pid_by_tx: t99-sidecar (pid 4211)
```
carmen: If softirq is stuck on one core we get qdisc buildup and tails. Two immediate low-risk moves: 1) spread IRQs across cores, 2) patch sidecar to add small jitter (50-200ms) to polling.

ivy: Thoughts on moving tenant-99 to a tiny dedicated slice as a bandaid? It'd isolate but costs more. What's our quick cost estimate?

rohan: Dedicated tiny-slice (single-GPU reserved) in this region ≈ 2x current marginal for that tenant during peak because of headroom and preprovision. Also scheduling/replication adds ~10%.

carmen: Let's avoid carveout unless customer impact persists >30m. Plan: (A) apply irq-affinity spread on affected hosts; (B) throttle sidecar via cgroup net_cls to 50mbit burst; (C) monitor 10m. If still >8ms, open escalation to support for carveout.

ops-bot: Action: irq-affinity-spread applied to r33-node[2-5] by automation (1839991120).

ivy: After irq spread p95 -> 6.2ms, tx_q_len -> 20. Good improvement. I'll roll the sidecar throttle canary now (helm patch `values.telemetry.poll_jitter: 120ms`).

rohan: Add follow-ups: - telemetry jitter default (owner: carmen) - auto-attr in alert pipeline to include top-pid/cgroup (owner: rohan) - cost calc doc for dedicated tiny-slices (owner: finance-eng)

carmen: Will file INFRA-2002 with configs + commands used. Also adding small snippet to runbook: `try irq spread -> 5m wait -> apply per-tenant throttle -> consider dedicated-tiny-slice` :white_check_mark:
